title: Stop refuses to end a turn with an open CI run and no check-in set
why:
CI waits have no enforcer: a session can end its turn on an open run with no check-in, and nothing wakes it. OWNER ITEMS 11:52 CST Nov 14 (lane ci-wait-stop-checkin-v2, draft #3410 which replaces #3063; message 11:43 CST; triage read none of its code): two questions are on the waiting page. Item 836 (pick-ci-wait-one-wait): the hook keeps one wait, the newest ready call; ready PR 5, ready PR 6, then a green line that names no PR closes the wait and PR 5 has no check-in while Stop passes (hooks/stall_watch.py open_ci_wait; reviewer round 1 probe). Option a keep one wait (starred at the lane's recommendation), b one wait per ready PR. Item 837 (pick-ci-wait-checkin-tools): the check counts CronCreate and any check-in covers the wait; test CI05 in hooks/test_stall_watch_stop.py pins it; the coordinator picked keep at 11:07 CST (undoable). Option a keep four tools (widens the check, not starred), b send_later only. Both are recorded Limits in decision ci-wait-reads-run-status; the lane does not wait. Owner ruling read by triage: own-ci-wait-subscribe-guard (subscribe or poll first; check-ins are the safety net), which names no tool and no wait count. DONE 14:39 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 14:42, REST 14:39; relayed; triage read no diff): #3063 (an undo or draft-again closes the CI wait; a branch-named wait closes on a merge of any PR) merged 14:38:37 CST as dff2cf430350d61b7c223af3e6725db40c4ba83d, alone on its green ready run 43635026510 (green 20:33:36Z). #3410 was closed as replaced earlier (archive/ci-wait-stop-checkin-v2). Owner items 836 (one wait or one per ready PR) and 837 (four check-in tools or send_later only) stay open. OWNER 18:37 CST Nov 14: on both items he picked none of these with a question: 836 "is B better", 837 "is B better but just needs to be better thought out?". Answered on the items (no pick, no star); the coordinator is asked for its view. Neither item is closed. COORDINATOR VIEW 18:45 CST Nov 14 on page items 836 and 837 (coordinator 18:43; its read-only Sonnet Explore agent read hooks/stall_watch.py, hooks/guard.py and this step at local main af2c312c, shallow, later edits unknown; triage read no code; unverified by triage). The Stop check counts send_later, create_trigger, CronCreate and ScheduleWakeup (stall_watch.py:862, tests CI03-CI06); it reads only the tool name (:975), never run_once_at, cron_expression or recurring, so a recurring check-in passes; it keeps ONE wait. The 55-minute cap guards only send_later with CI wording. Usage unmeasured except list_triggers 18:41: 2 one-shot, 0 recurring. 836: the coordinator recommends b (one wait per ready PR; case #3424 and #3425 in CI at once 18:02 to 18:15, n=1); star moved a to b. 837: it recommends neither a nor b; new option c (keep four tools, read each call, refuse create_trigger with cron_expression and CronCreate recurring) added and starred. Owner picks; no lane waits on either item. A lane to measure which tools sessions use to wait goes with the step once he picks. COORDINATOR READ 18:48 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 18:46): it read the full text of items 836 and 837; its 18:43 views hold (836 b, 837 new option c). Yes to a measuring lane: one bounded read of session transcripts for calls to the four waiting tools, by tool and kind (one-time or recurring); no timer, no new log; the lane goes with the item's step once the owner picks. Triage read no transcript. PICKS 20:20 CST Nov 14 (coordinator's picks under the owner's 20:18 CST words 'Nothing can't be undone don't wait on me'; not the owner's own; undoable; relayed by the coordinator 20:19, triage read no code): item 836 closed on b (one wait per ready PR; ruling coord-836-b-one-wait-per-ready-pr); item 837 closed on option d, send_later only for session waits and the four tools kept for event waits a session cannot poll (ruling coord-837-d-send-later-session-waits). Not built: a Stop check that tells a session wait from an event wait is unbuilt; first act of the lane: measure which tools sessions use to wait (one bounded read of transcripts by tool and kind) and read whether the check can tell the two waits apart.

11:45 CST Nov 15 (triage): owner answered page item 854 (taken-837-d-send-later) with "none of these" at 11:41:05 CST and the note "i was actually asking" (verbatim). Not a ruling: no pick on Keep or Overrule. PENDING ASK. Item 854 asked: keep or overrule the coordinator's pick coord-837-d-send-later-session-waits (option d, send_later only for a session's own waits; the four tools stay for event waits). The note's meaning is UNCLEAR. One thing it may point at: on the original item 837 the owner's 15:01 CST Nov 14 chat was a question, "are these my only options and which is good and why?", and his 20:18 CST words were "Nothing can't be undone don't wait on me"; the coordinator took d for him. Whether "actually asking" means he asked a question and wants an answer, or he never picked, is not read from any record. Triage guessed neither. The pick coord-837-d stands as a coordinator pick (undoable) until the owner says; the Stop-check build waits on nothing here.

A rule that waits on a check-in can stall when one never fires. If a platform cause is confirmed, it goes to step upstream-session-raises. Cause unknown; the step's check must not assume a check-in fires on time.
